indicators.flag: Customers frequently appear to move through, and transact from, different geographic locations in the United States.  These transactions can be combined with travel and transactions in and to foreign countries that are significant conduits for human trafficking.
indicators.red_flag: Multi-location domestic movement + travel/transactions into trafficking-conduit jurisdictions
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.flag: Transactions are inconsistent with a customer’s expected activity and/or line of business in an apparent effort to cover trafficking victims’ living costs, including housing (e.g., hotel, motel, short-term rentals, or residential accommodations), transportation (e.g., airplane, taxi, limousine, or rideshare services), medical expenses, pharmacies, clothing, grocery stores, and restaurants, to include fast food eateries.
indicators.red_flag: Out-of-pattern victim-living-cost spend (lodging / transport / medical / retail)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D4 (Card & merchant-category (MCC) transaction data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a card or account whose merchant-category spend distribution shifts toward high-risk or atypical MCCs for the customer's segment, escalating when spend concentrates in cash-equivalent categories such as gift cards, prepaid, or money-services merchants.
build_logic.window: rolling 60 days vs segment MCC baseline
build_logic.source: card authorization/settlement feed enriched with MCC reference
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: Transactional activity largely occurs outside of normal business operating hours (e.g., an establishment that operates during the day has a large number of transactions at night), is almost always made in cash, and deposits are larger than what is expected for the business and the size of its operations.
indicators.red_flag: Off-hours cash-heavy activity, deposits oversized vs business operations
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D1 (Core transaction monitoring (deposit/account ledger)), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a business account whose transaction inflows are disproportionate to its declared revenue, headcount, payroll, or operating-expense footprint relative to industry peers, escalating when revenue appears decoupled from any observable operational activity.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days vs declared profile and peer cohort
build_logic.source: business deposit ledger joined to KYC business profile + industry peer benchmarks
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: A customer frequently makes cash deposits with no Automated Clearing House (ACH) payments.
indicators.red_flag: Recurring cash deposits with no ACH (cash-only placement)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C5 (Cash-intensity / cash-placement anomaly detection); data D2.

indicators.flag: An individual frequently purchases and uses prepaid access cards.
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C5 (Cash-intensity / cash-placement anomaly detection); data D2.

indicators.flag: A customer’s account shares common identifiers, such as a telephone number, email, and social media handle, or address, associated with escort agency websites and commercial sex advertisements.
indicators.red_flag: Account identifiers matching escort-agency / commercial-sex-ad web presence
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.flag: Frequent transactions with online classified sites that are based in foreign jurisdictions.
indicators.red_flag: Frequent payments to foreign-based online-classified sites
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D5 (Transaction narrative / free-text fields), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A customer frequently sends or receives funds via cryptocurrency to or from darknet markets or services known to be associated with illicit activity.  This may include services that host advertising content for illicit services, sell illicit content, or financial institutions that allow prepaid cards to pay for cryptocurrencies without appropriate risk mitigation controls.
indicators.red_flag: Crypto flow to/from darknet markets and illicit-service VASPs
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: Frequent transactions using third-party payment processors that conceal the originators and/ or beneficiaries of the transactions.
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C16 (Third-party / nominee funding & legal-professional channel detection); data D3.

indicators.flag: A customer avoids transactions that require identification documents or that trigger reporting requirements.
indicators.red_flag: ID-document and reporting-trigger avoidance (structuring / KYC evasion)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C4 (Structuring / sub-threshold & reporting-trigger evasion).
